title: Downloadable Agents package system missing
reality: v2.3.0 restructured the agent architecture: a full-page Agents → Download Agents library installs/updates/uninstalls official capability packages from the Pasta-Devs/Marinara-Agents catalog (29 packages, grouped Writer/Tracker/Misc; Card Evolution=Writer, Hierarchical Maps=Tracker). Hierarchical Maps, Conversation audio/video calls, UNO, Chess, Poker, 8-Ball Pool, Tic-Tac-Toe, and Rock-Paper-Scissors moved out of the base Engine into optional packages with package-owned server runtimes; >25,000 lines removed from base, replaced by validated capability registries and compatibility bridges. Fresh installs contain NO optional agents; existing installs migrate selections. Install All/Uninstall All bulk controls exist. v2.3.1 added automatic startup upgrade of installed packages from the catalog with rollback on failure; v2.3.2 added capability API 1.3 host services (#3690) and Conversation/Roleplay/Game compatibility badges; v2.3.3 made catalog selection compatible per Engine major.
fix: Add a 'Downloadable Agents / packages (v2.3)' section to architecture.md covering the Download Agents library, the Marinara-Agents catalog repo, which features are now optional packages (Maps, Calls, six table games), fresh-installs-empty behavior, migration, startup auto-update, and capability API 1.3; update the Agent core-object entry to note many former built-ins are now downloadable packages.

title: Storage section still documents SQLite backend and DATABASE_URL import
reality: v2.3.0 'Removed the retired database compatibility stack, including its runtime backend switch, startup migrations, one-time importer and repair readers, old migration scripts, database-file backup handling, and external ORM/runtime dependencies. Storage schemas and query expressions are now file-native throughout the Engine.' There is no STORAGE_BACKEND=sqlite opt-in and no DATABASE_URL import path anymore. v2.3.0 also made file-native primary/natural-key constraints enforceable during atomic inserts/updates.
fix: In Data Storage, delete the sentences 'SQLite is a legacy opt-in (STORAGE_BACKEND=sqlite); DATABASE_URL is only consulted to import old data when DATA_DIR/storage doesn't yet exist.' State that as of v2.3.0 storage is file-native throughout — the runtime backend switch, migrations, importer, and ORM dependencies were removed — and note enforceable file-native primary/natural-key constraints.

title: Game Mode missing Tactical Combat Preference
reality: v2.3.0 added a Combat Preference to Game mode, chosen in the setup wizard and changeable later from Chat Settings → Combat Style: keep classic narrative combat, or switch to a tactical battle style inspired by grid-based tactics RPGs. Tactical encounters run on a terrain-painted battlefield with scene-matched backdrops, unit classes, party formations, per-unit movement/attack ranges, counters, crits, misses, and a full enemy phase driven by a deterministic seeded engine at four difficulty levels; animated movement, damage popups, draggable unit inspector/action menu, translucent staged-move previews, restartable encounters, mobile-friendly layout.
fix: In the Game Mode section, add a 'Tactical Combat (v2.3)' paragraph describing the Combat Preference (setup wizard + Chat Settings → Combat Style), the two styles (narrative vs tactical), the terrain battlefield, deterministic seeded engine, and four difficulty levels.

title: Game setup export is now a .marinara-game-setup.json bundle, not .txt
reality: v2.3.2 (#3701) changed Initial Game Setup downloads to versioned `.marinara-game-setup.json` bundles that can refill the New Game wizard, remap available local resources, warn about missing ones, and require a replacement GM connection when necessary. The v2.2-era plain `.txt` export described in the skill is superseded.
fix: In the 'Session History (v2.2)' paragraph of Game Mode, replace the '.txt' export description with the v2.3.2 reusable export/import: versioned .marinara-game-setup.json bundles importable into the New Game wizard with resource remapping, missing-resource warnings, and GM-connection replacement prompts.

title: Hierarchical Maps not documented
reality: Hierarchical Maps exists as a downloadable Tracker Agent package (v2.3.0) enableable in Roleplay and during/after Game creation, with a world-map surface and a full hierarchical map editor (#3691). v2.3.2 moved its controls inside its entry in Chat Settings → Agents (#3679). v2.3.3 fixed it to obey each chat's Enable Agents master toggle across UI, prompt generation, lorebook previews, retries, tracker patches, carryover, and checkpoints; quarantined incompatible Maps 1.0.x runtimes (the 't.select is not a function' crash); fixed the v2.3.2 migration that wrongly selected Maps in every Roleplay/VN/Game chat (#3723, one-time correction); and stopped pending Game tracker edits from calling Maps when inactive ('Failed to flush 1 game-state patch callback').
fix: Add Hierarchical Maps to architecture.md (Game/Roleplay sections or the new packages section): downloadable Tracker Agent package, per-chat enablement under Chat Settings → Agents, world-map + hierarchical map editor, gated by the Enable Agents master toggle, and note the 2.3.3 migration/quarantine fixes as known-issue context.

title: Noodle prompt override description outdated — editable Noodle Prompt
reality: v2.3.0 added an editable Noodle Prompt at the top of Noodle Settings with a full-screen editor and one-click default restoration. The canonical default now contains the complete adult-platform, persona-authorship, interaction, and JSON instructions, while the separate timeline voice text is appended last. The skill's claim that only a 'Noodle Timeline Voice & Tone' override is registerable while everything else stays hardcoded no longer reflects the user-facing model.
fix: In the Noodle Refresh paragraph, replace the Voice & Tone-only override description with the v2.3.0 editable Noodle Prompt (Noodle Settings, full-screen editor, default restore, timeline voice appended last).

title: Noodle refresh participant selection and 8192-token budgets missing
reality: v2.3.2 changed Noodle refreshes to choose active participants BEFORE first-time profile generation, skip characters that already have generated profiles, and send only the selected character cards to the timeline model; world/lore context and chat carryover each got an 8,192-token budget so large invited rosters cannot inflate unrelated generations.
fix: In Noodle's Refresh and Profiles paragraphs, note that participant selection happens before profile generation (only selected cards are sent, already-profiled characters skipped) and that world/lore context and chat carryover each have an 8,192-token budget (v2.3.2).

title: Noodle persona authorship preservation missing
reality: v2.3.1 preserved distinct Noodle authorship across persona switching: posts and replies retain their originating persona account and snapshot, timeline prompts identify each persona by handle and stable identity key, and chat carryover summaries name the persona account instead of collapsing activity into the currently selected identity.
fix: In the Noodle Accounts paragraph (account switcher), add that authorship is preserved per-persona across switching — posts/replies keep their originating persona, and carryover summaries name the persona account (v2.3.1).

title: Noodle Professor Mari exclusion setting missing
reality: v2.3.0 (#3598) added a default-ON Noodle setting that excludes Professor Mari from account discovery and future generated activity without deleting existing timeline history. The skill currently lists Professor Mari as a Noodle account with no mention that she is excluded by default.
fix: In the Noodle Accounts paragraph, note that Professor Mari participation is governed by a default-on exclusion setting (v2.3.0, #3598) — she is excluded from discovery and new generated activity unless the setting is changed; existing history is kept.

title: Conversation prompt assembly rework not documented
reality: v2.3.1 reworked Conversation prompt assembly: Peek Prompt groups Conversation turns under a Chat History section; character join/leave notices become timestamped history events only after a chat has started; reaction syntax lives inside a Commands section; merged-group speaker-prefix and character-only response boundaries are emitted last in the preset's XML/Markdown/plain output format; the built-in Conversation prompt and Marinara preset use identity wording fitting one-to-one and group chats, with a startup migration for old bundled presets.
fix: In 'Prompt Assembly (Simplified)', add a 'v2.3.1 Conversation assembly changes' note covering the Chat History grouping, timestamped join/leave events, Commands section for reaction syntax, and last-emitted merged-group response boundaries; also update the 'For conversation mode, assembly is simpler' sentence accordingly.

title: Conversation group chats now one merged generation per turn
reality: v2.3.1 restored Conversation group chats to a single merged provider generation per turn — the model chooses every present speaker within one grouped response instead of a separate restricted request per character (Roleplay Individual mode unchanged). v2.3.0 (#3609) also fixed Bubble display so each generated line gets its own bubble and unprefixed consecutive lines inherit the preceding speaker.
fix: Expand the 'Group DMs are supported — the engine picks who speaks next' line: as of v2.3.1 group Conversation turns are one merged generation in which the model voices all present speakers; note Roleplay Individual mode is unaffected.

title: Conversation schedule timezone selector missing
reality: v2.3.1 added a global timezone selector to Conversation schedule creation: defaults to browser-detected IANA timezone, can be overridden or reset to the device zone, syncs across devices, applies to existing and future Conversation chats; schedule generation, presence, autonomous messages, temporal prompt context, and background server polling honor it. Related v2.3.0 fix (#3590): blank TZ= now inherits the host timezone instead of Etc/Unknown.
fix: In Conversation Mode's Schedules bullet, add the v2.3.1 global IANA timezone selector and what honors it (schedules, presence, autonomous messages, temporal context, server polling).

title: Conversation About Me drafting moved to Professor Mari
reality: v2.3.2 moved Conversation About Me drafting from per-editor 'AI Write' controls to Professor Mari; Character and Persona Convo editors no longer expose a separate model connection or source settings — Mari inspects a saved character/persona, writes the bio in their voice, and saves directly to the About Me field. v2.3.0 also notes the About Me profile and update_about_me tool remain built into the Engine (not downloadable agents).
fix: Add to the Professor Mari section (or Conversation Mode) that About Me bios are now drafted via Professor Mari (v2.3.2), the per-editor AI Write controls were removed, and About Me/update_about_me stay built-in rather than packaged.

title: Roleplay persona-less chats behavior missing
reality: v2.3.2 fixed new Roleplay chats to stay Persona-less when the user selects no Persona — including the first optimistic message snapshot, provider prompt, scene generation, and combat context; only Conversation mode may fall back to the globally active Persona.
fix: In the Persona core-object entry or Roleplay Mode section, note that Roleplay chats with no selected Persona remain persona-less end-to-end (v2.3.2); only Conversation falls back to the globally active Persona.

title: Roleplay summary truncation limits removed
reality: v2.3.2 removed Roleplay Summary's 2,000-character per-source-message truncation and the 64 KiB compiled-summary ceiling in chats.json, so chapter-length messages and accumulated summaries remain complete unless the selected model rejects the request.
fix: In the 'Chat Summary (v2.2)' paragraph of Roleplay Mode, add that as of v2.3.2 the per-message 2,000-char truncation and 64 KiB compiled-summary ceiling were removed.

title: Conversation Calls renamed to Calls and made a downloadable package
reality: v2.3.2 renamed user-facing 'Conversation Calls' to 'Calls' (package IDs and legacy symbols preserved). v2.3.0 moved Conversation audio/video calls into an optional downloadable package; installed Calls settings render below Illustrator settings in Chat Settings and expand only after calls are enabled per chat. The skill still presents Calls as a built-in v2.1 feature under the old name.
fix: Rename 'Conversation Calls (v2.1)' references to 'Calls' (noting the old name and preserved package IDs), and state it is now an optional downloadable package (v2.3.0) rather than built-in.

title: Local Whisper is now owned by the Calls package
reality: v2.3.0 made Local Whisper a Calls-owned download: Connections shows Local Speech Model controls only while the Calls package is installed; uninstalling Calls removes every downloaded Whisper model and its saved selection; reinstalling restores download availability. v2.3.0 (#3671) also fixed downloaded models not being recognized when DATA_DIR was unset — capability runtimes now inherit the Engine's resolved host data directory.
fix: In the Voice input bullet under Calls, note local_whisper depends on the Calls package being installed (models are removed on uninstall) and that Whisper model storage inherits the Engine's resolved DATA_DIR (v2.3.0).

title: New env vars CHAT_GENERATION_TIMEOUT_MS and AUTO_UPDATE_ENABLED missing
reality: v2.3.3 (#3730) added CHAT_GENERATION_TIMEOUT_MS for slow Conversation, Roleplay, and Game providers, and AUTO_UPDATE_ENABLED=false for persistent launcher update opt-out on Windows, macOS/Linux, and Termux without disabling manual updates.
fix: Add CHAT_GENERATION_TIMEOUT_MS and AUTO_UPDATE_ENABLED to the env/config notes (near the VIDEO_GEN_TIMEOUT_MS list or a troubleshooting note), citing v2.3.3.

title: What's New window and generation-completion notifications missing
reality: v2.3.0 added a one-time, version-aware What's New window (post-onboarding, Professor Mari-narrated, links to the GitHub release, remembers the version shown) and separate opt-in browser/Android generation-completion notifications for manually started Conversation, Roleplay, Visual Novel, and Game replies finishing while Marinara is unfocused (#3588), without changing autonomous-message notification preferences.
fix: Add a brief bullet in 'Special Features Worth Knowing' covering the What's New window and the opt-in generation-completion notifications (v2.3.0).

title: Bot Browser renamed to Card Browser / Cards Library
reality: v2.3.0 renamed Bot Browser to Card Browser throughout the interface, docs, onboarding, and Professor Mari guidance, and renamed 'Browse Online' to 'Download Cards'; the browser opens as 'Cards Library' within the unified library shell. The skill still says characters are 'browsed from Chub.ai via the Bot Browser' and labels the endpoint list '/api/bot-browser/*'.
fix: Update the Character entry and the API-surface bullet to use 'Card Browser' (formerly Bot Browser) / 'Download Cards' naming, keeping the /api/bot-browser route path if unchanged but noting the UI rename (v2.3.0).

title: Turn games section presents packages as built-in shared engines
reality: v2.3.0 moved UNO, Chess, Poker, 8-Ball Pool, Tic-Tac-Toe, and Rock-Paper-Scissors into optional downloadable packages with package-owned server runtimes; fresh installs ship none. v2.3.2 fixed installed Conversation games to appear in the Commands controls (no separate Add Agent entries), activate without an Engine restart (#3699), and run without legacy activeAgentIds metadata. The skill still describes them as a built-in shared engine family in packages/shared/src/features/turn-games/.
fix: Update the Turn games bullet in Conversation Mode: the six games are now optional downloadable packages (v2.3.0), toggled via the Commands controls, hot-activating without restart; drop or caveat the packages/shared built-in framing.

title: Connection Defaults 'Illustrator' category renamed 'Images'
reality: v2.3.0 renamed the Connections 'Illustrator' defaults category to 'Images' and hid image/video generation settings plus /illustrate and /selfie commands until the Illustrator package is installed; selfie configuration was consolidated as 'Illustrator Settings' under Chat Settings → Agents. The skill's Connection entry still lists the v2.2 Defaults categories as 'Main, Agents, Illustrator, Videos'.
fix: In the Connection core-object entry, change the Defaults categories to 'Main, Agents, Images, Videos' (Images renamed from Illustrator in v2.3.0) and note Illustrator-dependent settings/commands only appear when the Illustrator package is installed.

title: Venice.ai missing from image generation providers
reality: v2.3.2 (#3682) added Venice.ai as an Image Generation service with authenticated live image-model discovery and native /image/generate support, model-aware sizing, and validated base64 responses.
fix: Add Venice.ai to the 'Image gen:' provider line in Providers Supported (v2.3.2).

title: Agents master toggle and per-mode custom agent availability missing
reality: v2.3.x formalized a per-chat Enable Agents master switch: v2.3.0 (#3669) preserved it during the capability migration so upgrades cannot silently reactivate agents; v2.3.2 (#3692) allowed selected custom agents to run in Conversation, Roleplay, and Game whenever Enable Agents is on while official packages keep per-mode availability rules; v2.3.3 made Hierarchical Maps obey it fully. Chat Settings → Agents stays available in all three modes even with no optional agents installed (v2.3.0).
fix: Document the per-chat Enable Agents master toggle in the Agent core-object entry or the new packages section, including that custom agents run in all three modes when it is on and official packages respect per-mode compatibility.
